title: Reliable compliance delivery: webhook backpressure handling and archival handoff
creator: Sonia Chen
description: Background: We need an operationally safe, observable, and auditable delivery mechanism for compliance events (residency assertions, retention-change, and legal-hold snapshots) that can survive transient receiver outages, variable downstream capacity, and regional failover. Current webhook fanout retries are simplistic and cause large bursts and duplicate deliveries when receivers recover. This ticket designs and implements: 1) a backpressure-aware delivery policy for webhooks, 2) a durable pending-queue with archival handoff for events that cannot be delivered within retention window, and 3) a compact, single-file evidence snapshot option for legal-hold/forensics that preserves residency metadata and cryptographic attestations.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Webhook sender honors per-consumer backpressure signals (429 Retry-After, 503 with Retry-After) and scales retries using an exponential backoff + full jitter strategy configurable per-customer. 2) Events that hit max retry window (configurable, default 72 hours) are atomically moved to a Durable Archive bucket and an archival notification event is emitted to the evidence pipeline. 3) Durable queue persists to S3 (or equivalent object store) with per-tenant prefix and encryption, and supports restart/replay without duplication guarantees. 4) Evidence snapshots (legal-hold) are produced as signed tarball files containing the original events, residency assertions, and a signed manifest. 5) Observability: per-tenant metrics for pending_queue_depth, delivery_latency_p95, archive_rate, and delivery_error_rate; alert if pending depth > threshold or archive rate spikes. 6) API contract changes documented and backwards-compatible with v1 endpoints.
design_decisions: - Use a two-layer delivery strategy: fast in-memory queue (for low-latency) backed by persistent object-store segments for durability. - Retry policy: base 15s, multiplier 2.0, max interval 30m, max elapsed 72h (configurable). Randomized full jitter per attempt to avoid thundering herd. - Honor both Retry-After header and our computed backoff; use the larger of the two. - On consumer-provided ‘pause’ webhook response (HTTP 423 with X-Resume-After header), shift consumer into paused state for given window. - Archival handoff: when event exceeds max elapsed or reaches TTL threshold, atomically move to s3://compliance-evidence/{region}/{tenant}/{date}/ and emit an internal archival-event to evidence-service with signed manifest URL. - Evidence snapshot format: gzipped tar containing events.jsonl, residency.json, manifest.sig (Ed25519 signature), and README.txt with provenance. - Idempotency: deliver using event_id + dedupe window; archive and durable queue operations are idempotent by key.
api_contract_example: POST /v2/compliance/events (producer -> RLZ delivery service)\nRequest JSON fields: event_id, created_at, tenant_id, event_type, payload_url, residency_zone, retention_ttl_seconds, legal_hold_tag (optional), signed_attestation_url (optional).\nDelivery semantics: RLZ attempts to POST to consumer endpoint with the event JSON expanded. On final archive, RLZ includes archival_manifest_url and archival_reason in the delivered archival-event. Backwards compatibility: consumers relying on v1 will still receive the original flattened fields; v2 includes residency_zone and signed_attestation_url.
implementation_notes: - New service module: rlz-delivery-service with two workers: fast-deliver-worker (in-memory) and durable-archiver-worker (object-store segments). - Use existing key-management integration to sign manifests (KMS). - Storage layout: segments of ~10k events per object to bound S3 object size and make replay efficient. - Dedupe store: Redis with 30d expiry per event_id for delivered events; fallback to RocksDB index on durable worker if Redis unavailable. - Schema evolution: add schema version header in event objects and support graceful parsing of unknown fields.
testing_and_qa: - Unit tests: retry timing, jitter distribution, and pause/resume behavior. - Integration tests: simulated consumer outage with controlled 502/429 responses; validate that delivery rate respects Retry-After and jitter. - Load test: 50k events/min with variable consumer latencies to validate queueing and archive behavior. - End-to-end test: legal-hold snapshot generation, signature verification (using test KMS key), and replay into evidence-search. - Run canary in eu-west-1 with 5 tenants for 72 hours before global rollout.
monitoring_and_slos: - Metrics to emit: rlz.delivery.attempts, rlz.delivery.success, rlz.delivery.failures, rlz.delivery.pended, rlz.archive.created, rlz.archive.bytes, rlz.paused_consumers_count. - SLO: 99.5% of events either delivered or archived within 72h; p95 delivery latency < 2s for healthy consumers. - Alerts: notify on sustained pending_queue_depth > 100k across region or archive_rate > 5% of incoming events for > 30m.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature flags behind 'rlz_new_delivery' and 'rlz_archive_handoff'. 2) Canary in eu-west-1 (5 tenants) for 72h. 3) Expand to all hosted tenants over 48h observing metrics. 4) Enable for Dedicated customers by request after manual review. 5) Deprecate old retry path 60 days after rollout completion with migration docs.
migration_path: - Consumers: no immediate action required. For advanced features (pause/resume, signed_manifest_url), consumers can opt-in to v2. - Internal: migrate pending events from old queue format by running one-time converter job that writes into new segment layout with identical keys. - Notify customers of archival behavior change via console banner and support ticket template.
open_questions: Should max elapsed default be 72h or 168h for enterprise customers?
Do we surface an admin API for tenant operators to purge archived bundles?
Policy for legal hold retention vs tenant-specified retention: precedence rules?
